newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Tofas to cut one shift from Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: Turk Tofas to cut one shift from Dec 2.

text.p: Turkey's leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi said it would reduce production from two shifts to one from December 2 and make 1,011 workers redundant from January 2, 1997.

In a statement sent to the Istanbul Stock Exchange, Tofas said the 1,011 workers would be put on compulsory leave from the beginning of December and would receive 76 percent of their normal wage until January 2, 1997.

An official from the labour union Turk Metal in Bursa where Tofas's plant is located, had said on Wednesday that the 1,011 workers, or 22 percent of the company's workforce, would be put on compulsory leave with half pay from November 22.
The union official said the reason the workers' redundancy was being delayed until 1997 was so that they could earn higher redundancy payments, having completed another full year's work.
Tofas announced on Wednesday its single-shift and layoff plans in the face of falling demand amid expectations of cheaper car imports after a recent cabinet decree to ease import rules.
Tofas is equally owned by Italian Fiat Spa and leading Turkish industrial group Koc Holding with each holding a 37.86 percent stake.
The one shift reduction will lead to a 30 percent drop in the production capacity of Tofas which already uses less than half of its capacity due to weak demand.
Car and parts producers as well as labour unions in Turkey's automotive sector have been strongly opposing the decree which went into effect on October 24.

The decree allows some three million expatriate Turkish workers in Europe to import cars and machinery of up to four years of age without customs duties, if they deposit a minimum of 50,000 marks for one year at state-owned Ziraat Bank.

Those who open the minimum account by end-1996 can bring in one duty free foreign car or 50,000 marks worth of machinery from June 1, 1997. They will also receive 10 percent annual interest on their deposits.

Such accounts totalling 42 million marks have so far been opened at Ziraat Bank. The government forecasts 25,000 duty free car imports in 1997 and an income of 1.25 billion marks from the scheme as part of its two revenue raising packages.
Turkey's car output plunged 32 percent from a year ago to 17,350 units in October and fell by seven percent to 172,964 in January-October, compared to the same 1995 period.
